All imported findings MUST be normalized to the canonical finding model and MUST pass through the shared deduplication pipeline.
Import MUST classify each finding by asset class, and infrastructure-class findings MUST NOT contribute to application security posture scores.
Import MUST be idempotent on a submission identity derived from content and target, such that resubmitting the same file does not duplicate findings or create a second import record.
Import MUST execute asynchronously with observable progress, and MUST accept files up to a configured size limit with rejection above it.

Import MUST define and implement partial-failure semantics: valid records MUST be ingested, invalid records MUST be quarantined with a per-record reason, and the import MUST report a per-record outcome summary.
Quarantined records MUST be retrievable, correctable, and re-submittable without re-importing the whole file.
Import MUST resolve each finding to an asset anchor, and MUST create assets in an unclaimed state rather than discarding findings whose asset cannot be resolved.
The platform MUST record import provenance for every finding: source file identity, importing principal, parser and parser version, and import timestamp.
The platform MUST support reversal of an import, returning affected findings to their prior state where they were modified by that import and removing those it created.
Generic tabular and structured import MUST support tenant-defined, reusable field mapping templates with a preview step before commitment.

The platform MUST support migration import of work item history from an incumbent tracker, preserving item identity, state history, comments with original authorship and timestamps, attachments, and links, and MUST record every migrated record as migrated with its original external identifier.
Every export MUST enforce the requesting principal's authorized scope at generation time, and MUST NOT include any record outside it.
Exports MUST exclude credentials, secret values, and raw evidence content without exception, regardless of the requesting principal's permissions.
Exports exceeding a configured record threshold MUST execute asynchronously with delivery via an authenticated, expiring reference.
Export operations MUST be audit-logged with the requesting principal, applied scope, record count, format, and generation timestamp.
The platform MUST support export in tabular, structured, and document formats, and MUST support export of a saved query's result set.
Every finding MUST be created through this pipeline. No component outside Ingestion MUST write a finding fingerprint.
Pipeline stages MUST be observable per session, with per-stage record counts and durations.
A field absent in the source MUST be null. A parser MUST NOT infer, default, or synthesize a value not present.
The source record MUST be retained per finding, and reprocessing under a new parser version MUST be possible from it without re-importing the file.
location_hint MUST NOT participate in fingerprint computation.
Parsers MUST be registered definitions, not code branches in a shared import service.
Every parser MUST declare its version, and the version MUST be recorded per finding.

Each parser MUST have a fixture corpus covering: a valid document, an empty document, a malformed document, a document at each declared limit, a document with absent optional fields, and one per known source-tool version.
A source format version not in a parser's declared support list MUST be rejected with the supported versions named, not parsed on a best-effort basis.
An SBOM arriving through file upload MUST be routed to the SBOM submission path, not parsed into findings.
A finding whose asset cannot be resolved MUST create an unclaimed asset, and MUST NOT be discarded or rejected.
Anchor resolution MUST record which step resolved it, and resolution by creation MUST be distinguishable from resolution by match.
Where a source provides an organization scope, it MUST be re-validated against the importing principal's authorized scope and MUST NOT be trusted from the file.
asset_class MUST be assigned by the parser and MUST NOT be tenant-configurable per finding.
Container findings MUST be classified by subject: application dependency findings as APPLICATION, base image and operating system findings as INFRASTRUCTURE.
Deduplication MUST compare only within the same tenant and the same fingerprint algorithm version.
Re-detection MUST NOT change finding state.
Suppression MUST be evaluated before finding creation, and a suppressed candidate MUST be recorded rather than silently dropped.
Where a fingerprint algorithm version changes, re-fingerprinting MUST be a migration from retained inputs that preserves triage state, assignment, comments, exceptions, and history.
A parse failure MUST ingest nothing. Partial parse results MUST NOT be normalized.
Quarantined records MUST be retrievable with their raw content and failing reason, correctable, and resubmittable without re-importing the source.
An unmappable severity MUST produce UNKNOWN and MUST be reported as a mapping gap, not defaulted to a middle value.
Session outcome MUST report per-record counts by disposition — ingested, updated, reopened, suppressed, quarantined, merged — and MUST NOT report only a total.
Reversal MUST restore prior state, not delete. A finding modified by the import MUST return to its earlier state rather than disappearing.
Reversal MUST be bounded to a configurable window and MUST require a permission distinct from import.
Reversal MUST be audited, and reversed findings MUST be recorded rather than erased.
Tabular import MUST support reusable versioned mapping templates.
A preview MUST be presented before commitment, showing the mapped result for a sample and the disposition counts the import would produce.
A mapping producing an anchor-creation rate above a threshold MUST warn before commitment.
Migration MUST preserve original authorship and original timestamps on comments and state transitions.
Migrated records MUST be flagged as migrated with their original external identifier, and the flag MUST survive into every presentation.
Authorship MUST map to platform principals where resolvable and to a clearly marked unresolved placeholder otherwise. It MUST NOT be attributed to an arbitrary existing principal.
Migration MUST be executed under an elevated permission distinct from import, MUST require step-up authentication, and MUST NOT bypass scope validation.
Migration MUST report per-record fidelity: fields carried, fields dropped, and authorship unresolved.
Scope MUST be applied at generation, not by filtering a broader result set.
Credentials, secret values, and evidence content MUST be excluded from every export format, at every permission level, without exception.
Per-person workload data MUST be excluded unless the requesting principal holds the restricted permission, and its inclusion MUST be separately audited.
Every export MUST embed its applied scope, filters, record count, and generation time in the artifact.
Exports above a configured record threshold MUST execute asynchronously with delivery by an authenticated expiring reference bound to the requesting principal's scope at generation.
Export MUST support tabular, structured, and document formats, and MUST support exporting a saved query's result set.
Export operations MUST be audited with principal, applied scope, record count, format, and generation time.
The platform MUST support tenant-authored knowledge articles with versioning, review dates, and ownership.
Knowledge articles MUST be linkable to finding classes, weakness classifications, asset types, and checklist items, and the linked guidance MUST surface in context.
The platform MUST support internal standards, secure development guidance, and control requirement content, mapped to the assessment checklists that verify them.
Knowledge content MUST be searchable alongside work items and findings, scope-filtered where content is scoped.
The platform MUST record which knowledge content was referenced in remediation and assessment activity.
Knowledge content MUST be usable as grounding for AI remediation guidance, with citation to the source article.
Knowledge content MUST support internationalization of both platform-supplied and tenant-authored articles.
The platform MUST maintain a catalogue of notifiable events, each declaring its default audience, default channels, and whether it is digestible or immediate.

The platform MUST generate notifications from domain events, including assignment, mention, state change on watched items, comment on watched items, approaching and breached service levels, information requests, and integration failures.
The platform MUST support delivery through in-product, email, and outbound integration channels, with channel selection per event category per user.
The platform MUST support digest delivery aggregating multiple events into a single scheduled notification, configurable per user.
The platform MUST deduplicate and coalesce notifications such that a burst of related events produces one notification rather than one per event.
The platform MUST support configurable escalation chains triggered by elapsed time without required action.
Notification content MUST be evaluated against the recipient's authorized scope at delivery time, and MUST NOT include data the recipient is not authorized to see.
Notifications MUST NOT include credentials, secret values, evidence content, or personal workload data.
Notification templates MUST be tenant-configurable and MUST support localization.
The platform MUST provide an in-product notification centre with read state and the ability to act directly from a notification.
The platform MUST record delivery outcome per notification and MUST surface persistent delivery failure to an administrator.
Users MUST be able to unsubscribe from any non-mandatory notification category, and the platform MUST define which categories are mandatory.
Notification MUST be produced by subscribing to domain events, and a domain transaction MUST NOT depend on notification success.
Content MUST be rendered per recipient with scope evaluated at render time, and a single rendered artifact MUST NOT be delivered to multiple recipients.
Every notifiable event MUST be catalogued with default audience, digestibility, and mandatory status, and an uncatalogued event MUST NOT produce a notification.
Digestibility and mandatory status MUST be product-fixed. Tenants MAY adjust audience and channel only.
Mandatory categories MUST NOT be unsubscribable, and break_glass.activated and audit.integrity_failed MUST additionally be non-suppressible by any in-product configuration.
The in-product channel MUST always be enabled and MUST NOT be disableable per user or per event.
Channel selection MUST be per event category per recipient, not global per recipient.
Principals MUST be able to unsubscribe from any non-mandatory category, and the platform MUST provide a single control to reduce non-mandatory volume without affecting mandatory categories.
Quiet hours MUST defer non-mandatory notifications and MUST NOT suppress mandatory ones.
Automatic subscription on assignment, comment, or mention MUST be unsubscribable per item.
A bulk operation, import, or automation execution MUST produce at most one summary notification per recipient, never one per affected item.
Events within the coalescing window for the same recipient and object MUST merge, and the merged notification MUST state the net change rather than the sequence.
Digest delivery MUST be configurable per recipient and MUST group by object rather than by event time.
Escalation MUST NOT fire against the accountable team while a clock is paused for requester or third-party blocking. A separate chain MUST escalate the blocking party.
Escalation MUST record each step fired so that a step is not repeated and the escalation history is auditable.
Escalation targets MUST be resolved at fire time, not at clock start.
Notification content MUST be evaluated against the recipient's authorized scope at delivery time, and MUST NOT include data the recipient is not authorized to see at that moment.
Notification content MUST NOT include credentials, secret values, evidence content, or per-person workload data, at any permission level or channel.
Where a recipient's scope has narrowed such that the notification's subject is no longer visible to them, the notification MUST be suppressed rather than sent with content removed.
External-channel content MUST default to minimal — subject identity and a link — with detail included only where the tenant has enabled it per category.
Templates MUST be tenant-configurable per event and channel, and MUST be validated to reference only fields available in the event's payload.
Templates MUST be localizable, and content MUST be rendered in the recipient's locale with locale-aware dates, times, and numbers in the recipient's timezone.
Template content MUST be treated as data, never as an executable template with access to platform internals.
Tenant vocabulary overrides MUST apply to notification content.
Inbound email MUST be associated with the originating item via an unguessable token in the reply address, and MUST NOT rely on the subject line or sender address for association.
The inbound token MUST identify the item, the recipient, and the notification, MUST expire, and MUST be single-purpose — it MUST NOT confer any authorization beyond posting a comment on that item.
Inbound content MUST be sanitized, MUST have quoted history and signatures stripped, and MUST be attributed to the identified recipient with the inbound origin recorded.
Where a reply cannot be associated, the sender MUST receive a failure response.
Immediate-category notifications MUST be dispatched within 60 seconds of the triggering event at p95.
Delivery MUST be retried with backoff on transient failure, MUST record outcome per notification, and MUST surface persistent failure to a tenant administrator.
A new or changed delivery address MUST be verified before notification content is sent to it.
Per-recipient rate limiting MUST apply, and exceeding it MUST force digest rather than discard.
Where every external channel for a recipient is failing or muted, mandatory notifications MUST remain visible in the in-product channel and the condition MUST be surfaced to the recipient.
The platform MUST represent organizational structure as a single hierarchy of OrgNode records of arbitrary depth, with node types defined per tenant.
Hierarchy traversal MUST be supported by a closure table or equivalent structure permitting ancestor and descendant resolution in a single query at any depth.
Each OrgNode MUST have exactly one parent, except tenant-root nodes which have none. Cycles MUST be rejected at write time.
Node types MUST be tenant-defined, each declaring its permitted parent types, whether it may own assets, and whether it may be a work item scope.
The platform MUST support tenant vocabulary override for node type labels and for platform-wide terms in the user interface, notifications, and reports.
Each OrgNode MUST carry a business criticality classification, either assigned directly or inherited from its nearest ancestor with an assignment.
Criticality inheritance MUST be overridable at any node, with the override recorded together with a justification and the acting user.
Each OrgNode MUST support one or more accountable owners, distinguishing business accountability from technical accountability.

The platform MUST support node lifecycle states of at least ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, and ARCHIVED, and MUST NOT permit hard deletion of a node that has ever had findings, assets, or work items associated with it.
The platform MUST support reorganization operations — moving a node with its subtree, merging two nodes, and splitting a node — as first-class, audited operations.

When an OrgNode is moved, merged, or split, the platform MUST preserve the scope context in effect at the time of each historical event, such that authorization decisions and aggregate reporting for past periods remain correct and reproducible.
The platform MUST support bulk import and ongoing synchronization of the organization hierarchy from an external authoritative source, with conflict reporting.
The platform MUST expose, for any user, the complete resolved set of nodes within their authorized scope, and MUST make that resolution available for inspection by administrators.
Changes to hierarchy structure, node criticality, ownership, and vocabulary MUST be audit-logged with actor, before value, after value, and timestamp.
Blocks 1, 2, and 4, and the transition log of block 7, MUST be delivered before any capability that writes data those mechanisms would have recorded.
Each phase MUST be independently usable, and a phase MUST NOT depend on a later phase to deliver value.
Phase P4 MUST include a measured adoption check: whether work-item conversation occurs in the platform or elsewhere.
Descoping MUST remove whole capabilities from §6, and MUST NOT relax individual requirements within a retained capability.
Where a capability is descoped, the mechanisms that capture data it would consume MUST still be delivered where that data cannot be reconstructed.
Descoping decisions MUST be recorded as decisions with their impact analysis, not as backlog deferrals.
Onboarding MUST be deliverable as a documented, repeatable procedure with the mapping templates and import artifacts it requires.
Imported historical data whose coverage is unknown MUST be recorded as unknown coverage, not as complete.
The operational store and toolchain decisions MUST be made against the disqualifying constraints of §8.1 before block 1 begins.
Hash partition counts MUST be fixed before the first production data, and the decision MUST be recorded with the sizing basis used.
A release candidate MUST NOT ship with any MUST_HAVE requirement lacking a passing test, or with any untraced schema object or API operation.
The requirement register MUST be regenerated and the corpus validated as a release gate.
Every accepted residual risk MUST be reviewed when its revisit trigger condition occurs, and the review outcome MUST be recorded.
Each release MUST record which deferred capabilities remain deferred and whether their reserved extension points are still valid.
The platform MUST be subject to its own assessment regime before commercial release, including penetration testing covering every scenario of DOC-26 §7.
Any authenticated user MUST be able to create a test request scoped to the organization nodes they are assigned.
Project selection MUST be filtered server-side to the caller's authorized scope, and the selected scope MUST be re-validated server-side on write, independently of the client-supplied identifier.
The platform MUST require at least two test accounts for each declared role before a request may be accepted.

Test account credentials MUST be stored in a secrets vault referenced by the request, MUST be masked by default in all interfaces, MUST require an explicit audited action to reveal, and MUST be excluded from every export format without exception.
Request attachments MUST be validated by content signature against declared type, malware-scanned before becoming retrievable, stored on an isolated origin, and served non-inline.
API collection and specification files MUST be parsed in a hardened parser with external reference resolution disabled, document depth and size limits, and safe deserialization.
The platform MUST derive an endpoint inventory from uploaded API collections, validate it against the declared endpoint count, and surface material discrepancies to the requester at submission time.
Requests MUST capture a required completion date and, where applicable, a go-live date.
The platform MUST require completion of an environment readiness attestation before a request may be accepted.
Any SLA clock MUST pause while a request is in a state awaiting action from the requester or a third party, with the pause reason recorded.
The platform MUST determine applicable checklist profiles and required specialist review tracks from intake classification.
The platform MUST flag test accounts for rotation or disablement at engagement closure and MUST require attestation of completion.
Requests MUST capture explicit in-scope and out-of-scope items and prohibited actions.
Requests MUST capture the specific code revision or release identifier to be tested.

Requests MUST capture exposure level, business criticality, personal data handling with volume indication, payment data handling, presence of AI or machine learning components, whether authentication or authorization logic changed, and third-party integration involvement.
Requests MUST capture test environment details including protective-control presence, and where a protective control is present the request MUST record an approved bypass or allowlist arrangement.
The platform MUST estimate effort from the request's technical profile using a deterministic, versioned model, and MUST record actual effort for subsequent calibration.
The platform MUST compute and display an earliest feasible start date from current backlog and capacity at submission time, and MUST warn where it is incompatible with the requester's required date.

External assessor access MUST be granted per engagement by explicit object grant, MUST NOT be derived from organizational scope inheritance, MUST be time-boxed with automatic revocation at engagement closure or grant expiry, MUST require acceptance of applicable agreements before first access, and MUST be audited at elevated granularity.
The platform MUST detect probable duplicate requests at submission and offer linking or merging.
Where testing spans multiple projects, the platform MUST model this as a request group containing one request per project rather than one request with multiple project scopes.
The platform MUST verify test account validity before engagement start and MUST transition the request to a blocked state with a paused clock where accounts are unusable.
Requests MUST record a technical contact, a business contact, and an escalation contact reachable during the test window.
The platform MUST support configurable approval gates before a request enters the security team's backlog.
The platform MUST surface, at intake, existing unresolved findings of significant severity on the target's assets.
Risk scores MUST be computed deterministically from recorded inputs. AI MUST NOT participate in score computation.
The scoring model MUST be versioned, and every computed score MUST record the model version, the input values, and the computation timestamp.
Risk scores MUST incorporate, at minimum: finding severity, exploit likelihood, known-exploited status, asset exposure, asset business criticality, and data sensitivity.
Factor weights MUST be tenant-configurable within validated bounds; the model's factor set and structural form MUST be product-fixed.
The platform MUST provide a factor-level explanation of any score, showing each factor's input value and contribution.
The platform MUST reproduce any historical score from its recorded inputs and model version.
When a score changes, the platform MUST identify which input changed and the resulting delta.
The platform MUST compute aggregate posture scores at any organization node, normalized for portfolio size and criticality composition to support comparison.
Aggregate scores MUST incorporate and display the coverage and freshness of their underlying data.

The platform MUST implement controls against score manipulation, at minimum: audited severity override, distinguished closure reasons, exception visibility in scored posture, and detection of anomalous bulk state changes.
The platform MUST support tenant-configurable service level policies mapping finding characteristics to remediation deadlines.
Service level computation MUST be business-calendar aware, supporting per-tenant working days, holidays, and time zones.
Service level clocks MUST support pause with recorded attribution, and elapsed paused time MUST be reportable separately.
The platform MUST detect approaching and breached service levels and MUST trigger configurable escalation.
The platform MUST support recorded, approved extension of a service level deadline, distinct from breach.
The formula MUST be a weighted sum of normalized factors modified by a contextual multiplier derived as the maximum of the contextual factors, with a floor preventing a zero multiplier.
Every factor MUST normalize to [0, 1] before weighting, and every normalization MUST be recorded with the score.
Where a factor's input is unavailable, the platform MUST apply a documented fallback and MUST record that the fallback was used. It MUST NOT silently substitute zero.
Scores MUST be presented as bands with the numeric value secondary.
Weights MUST be validated against per-factor bounds at configuration time, and an out-of-bounds configuration MUST be rejected with a specific diagnosis.

Weight changes MUST require elevated permission distinct from operational permissions, MUST be audited with before and after values, and MUST NOT take effect on existing scores until an explicit recomputation is initiated.
The platform MUST support previewing the effect of a weight change on a sample of the tenant's findings before activation.
A score MUST record sufficient input detail that its value can be recomputed identically without access to any other data, including data that has since changed.
Scores MUST be immutable. A recomputation creates a new score, and the prior score MUST be retained for the configured retention period.

Score change attribution MUST identify the changed inputs and their contribution to the delta, and MUST distinguish a change caused by population shift from one caused by a change to the finding or its asset.
Where an aggregate posture score improves, the platform MUST determine whether the improvement is attributable to remediation or to reduced coverage, and MUST present the distinction.
Every aggregate score MUST carry a coverage qualifier, and a score at INSUFFICIENT confidence MUST be presented as a coverage gap rather than as a posture figure.
Coverage MUST NOT be improvable by any action other than acquiring data. In particular, retiring or excluding unmeasured assets MUST NOT raise the coverage ratio.
Node-level posture MUST NOT be a sum of finding scores. It MUST be size-normalized and MUST include an explicit penalty for unmeasured scope.
Comparative presentation MUST state the normalization applied and the coverage of each compared entity.
Comparative presentation MUST enforce a minimum comparison-set size or suppress.
A clock MUST pin its policy version at start, and a later policy change MUST NOT move an existing deadline.
Duration MUST be computed in business time using the tenant's configured calendar and timezone, and calendar changes MUST NOT retroactively alter existing due dates.
Pausing MUST require a blocking attribution from an enumerated set, and paused time MUST be reportable separately from elapsed time.
Where a score increases such that a shorter policy applies, the platform MUST recompute the deadline from the original start using the new policy, and MUST NOT restart the clock.
Where a score decreases, the deadline MUST NOT be extended automatically. Extension MUST require an approved, recorded action.
Escalation MUST NOT fire while a clock is paused for requester or third-party blocking.
Effort estimation MUST be deterministic and versioned, and AI MUST NOT produce the estimate.
The platform MUST record estimated against actual effort and MUST expose estimation bias by assessment type and platform type.

Estimates MUST carry a confidence indication derived from the volume of calibration data for that type, and MUST be presented as low-confidence below a configured threshold of completed comparable items.

The platform MUST detect and surface anomalous rates of score-reducing actions — bulk closure as not-applicable, severity downgrade, criticality downgrade, exposure downgrade, suppression, and retirement — per principal and per organization node.
Reporting MUST distinguish verified remediation from other closure reasons wherever a closure or improvement figure is presented.

Score-affecting configuration — weights, thresholds, criticality tiers, service level policies — MUST require elevated permission, MUST be audited, and MUST be reported in a periodic configuration-change summary.

Score explanation MUST be generated from the recorded factor breakdown, and any generated explanation reaching a conclusion inconsistent with the recorded contributions MUST be rejected by output validation rather than presented.
A non-AI factor breakdown presentation MUST be available for every score, independently of AI availability.

The scoring model MUST be validated against the tenant's own historical finding data before a weight configuration is activated for production use, and the validation outcome MUST be recorded with the model version.
The platform MUST expose the concordance between score ranking and practitioner-assigned priority, as an ongoing model quality measure.
Matching MUST execute asynchronously as a background operation. No synchronous matching endpoint SHALL be exposed.
The platform MUST support batch matching over a scope-based selection with configurable concurrency, defaulting to one concurrent operation.
Interactive and batch matching MUST use isolated queue classes such that interactive operations are never blocked behind a batch.
Batch ordering MUST be weighted by asset business criticality and by time since last successful match, not first-in-first-out.
SBOM snapshots MUST be immutable, content-hash identified, and associated with an artifact identity and where available a revision identifier.
The platform MUST NOT execute project build tooling or dependency resolution.
The platform MUST NOT close findings on the basis of a match operation that did not complete successfully with confirmed coverage, and MUST NOT close findings where intelligence data was stale.
Match results MUST flow through the same normalization and deduplication pipeline as ingested scanner results.
Match operations MUST use lease-based work claiming with automatic reclamation of expired leases and bounded retry with backoff.
Every match operation MUST record the vulnerability intelligence version used, and the platform MUST support offline intelligence provisioning for air-gapped deployment.

The platform MUST expose an authenticated API accepting SBOM submissions, associating each with an organization scope and a build artifact identity. Manual upload MUST be available as a fallback. The platform MUST NOT acquire SBOMs by any other automated means in this release.

The platform MUST validate submitted SBOMs against format conformance and completeness criteria, MUST compute and expose a quality score, MUST reject submissions below a configurable rejection threshold, and MUST warn on submissions below an acceptance threshold. A submission containing zero components MUST be rejected.
The platform MUST re-match stored snapshots against updated vulnerability intelligence without requiring resubmission, and MUST do so automatically on intelligence update.
The platform MUST support on-demand re-matching for a selected scope, initiated by an authorized user.
The platform MUST compute a component change set between consecutive snapshots of the same artifact, identifying added, removed, and version-changed components.

Findings closed by automatic match-based resolution MUST record the resolving snapshot, the previous and current component versions, and the intelligence version, and MUST be distinguishable from human-verified closure.
The platform MUST expose SBOM coverage as a first-class metric: assets and organization nodes with no SBOM ever submitted, distinguished from those with current data.
The platform MUST compute SBOM age per asset and MUST support tenant-configurable freshness service levels by business criticality, with breach surfaced as a coverage gap.
Every metric, dashboard element, and report section derived from SBOM data MUST display the coverage and freshness of the data supporting it.
The platform MUST maintain queues of assets with no SBOM and assets with stale SBOMs, with configurable escalation to accountable owners.
The platform MUST expose submission health per integration credential, including last successful submission, failure count, and last failure reason.
Submission MUST re-validate the submitted project reference against the credential's pinned scope and MUST NOT trust it from the payload.

Where the named artifact does not exist in the asset graph, submission MUST create it in an UNCLAIMED state and queue it for ownership resolution. It MUST NOT reject the submission and MUST NOT silently discard it.
Submission MUST return the computed quality score and every warning in the response body, not only in a server-side log.
Submission MUST be rate-limited per credential, and the limit MUST accommodate the platform's own documented reference integration pattern without throttling.
A submission with zero components MUST be rejected.
Quality thresholds MUST be tenant-configurable within product-defined bounds, and the rejection threshold MUST NOT be configurable below the product floor.
The quality score MUST be computed by the platform from the document and MUST NOT be accepted from the submitter.
Quality score MUST be visible on the asset and in coverage reporting, and an asset whose latest snapshot is below the warning threshold MUST be treated as partially covered rather than covered.
A snapshot MUST be immutable after acceptance, and its identity MUST be its content hash. Resubmitting identical content MUST return the existing snapshot rather than creating a second.
The platform MUST retain snapshot history per artifact for a configurable period sufficient to compute change sets and to reproduce a historical match result.
Components MUST be stored canonicalized per ecosystem, with the original identifier retained alongside.
Canonicalization MUST be per-ecosystem, deterministic, and versioned, and the version MUST be recorded on every match run.
A component whose identifier cannot be canonicalized MUST be recorded as unmatchable with the reason, and MUST count against the snapshot's quality score. It MUST NOT be silently skipped.
Version comparison MUST use the ordering rules of the component's ecosystem, and the platform MUST NOT apply a single comparison scheme across ecosystems.
Where the platform cannot determine ordering for a component's version scheme, it MUST record the match as INDETERMINATE rather than asserting either presence or absence.
Where distribution-level patch metadata is available, it MUST take precedence over upstream version range comparison.

The test corpus MUST include, per supported ecosystem, cases covering pre-release ordering, epoch and revision components, boundary inclusivity, disjoint affected ranges, and backported patch metadata.
Exploitability statements MUST be applied at match time, and a suppressed candidate MUST be recorded as suppressed with the statement reference rather than omitted.

Statements authored by the tenant MUST be stored in the tenant's partition. Supplier-published statements accompanying a component MAY be shared as public data, and authorship MUST be recorded per statement.
Intelligence updates MUST trigger a portfolio re-match automatically, without requiring resubmission.
Batch ordering MUST be weighted by asset business criticality and by time since last successful match, and MUST NOT be arrival order.
A known-exploited catalogue update MUST take priority over an ordinary intelligence update sweep.
A match run MUST be idempotent on a key derived from snapshot content hash, intelligence version, matcher version, and canonicalization version.
A run MUST hold a lease with expiry and automatic reclamation, and MUST NOT rely on heartbeat liveness alone.
A batch sweep MUST be pausable and resumable without losing completed work, and MUST report progress including skipped and failed counts.

Where snapshot content hash, intelligence version, matcher version, and canonicalization version are all unchanged since the last successful run, the run MAY be skipped, and the skip MUST be recorded as a run with outcome SKIPPED_NO_CHANGE.
The platform MUST compute a component change set between consecutive snapshots and MUST surface newly introduced vulnerable components distinctly from long-standing ones.
A downgrade MUST be surfaced explicitly.
A match run MUST NOT drive finding closure unless it completed successfully, with confirmed coverage, against non-stale intelligence, over a snapshot whose quality is above the warning threshold.

Automatic closure MUST record the resolving snapshot, the previous and current component versions, the intelligence version, and the matcher version, and MUST be distinguishable from human-verified closure in every report.
Where a component is absent from a new snapshot but the snapshot's ecosystem coverage does not include that component's ecosystem, the finding MUST NOT be closed.
An asset with no snapshot MUST appear in coverage reporting as NEVER_SUBMITTED, and MUST NOT be absent from dependency reporting.
Every figure derived from composition data MUST be accompanied by the coverage and freshness of the data supporting it, materialized with the figure rather than computed at presentation.
The platform MUST maintain actionable queues for NEVER_SUBMITTED, STALE, and PARTIAL assets, with escalation to the accountable owner.
Submission health MUST be observable per credential, including last successful submission, consecutive failure count, and last failure reason.
Coverage MUST NOT be improvable by any action other than acquiring data. Retiring, excluding, or reclassifying unmeasured assets MUST NOT raise a coverage ratio.
Every match run MUST record the intelligence dataset version used, and staleness MUST be surfaced on findings produced or confirmed by that run.
The platform MUST support offline provisioning of intelligence through a signed bundle whose signature and integrity are verified before use.
Intelligence update failure MUST NOT halt matching. Matching MUST continue against the last verified version with staleness recorded.
Intelligence age MUST be visible in the interface and MUST alert beyond a configured threshold.
No failure in this module MUST result in finding closure, coverage improvement, or a favourable posture change.

Every tenant-scoped record MUST carry a tenant identifier, and isolation MUST be enforced at the persistence layer such that omitting a tenant predicate in application code cannot return cross-tenant data.
Tenant data MUST be encrypted at rest with per-tenant key material, and key access MUST be scoped to the tenant.

The platform MUST support tenant-level data residency pinning, and MUST enforce that pinned data does not leave its designated region including through backup, logging, telemetry, notification, and AI provider paths.
Tenant configuration, including roles, workflows, custom fields, taxonomies, scoring weights, and vocabulary, MUST be isolated per tenant with no shared mutable state.

No operation MUST span tenants, including background jobs, search, aggregation, AI context assembly, and export. Cross-tenant aggregation MUST require explicit tenant opt-in and MUST be irreversibly anonymised.
The platform MUST enforce per-tenant resource controls preventing one tenant's usage from degrading another's service.
Tenant lifecycle operations — provisioning, suspension, reactivation, and offboarding — MUST be supported as audited operations with defined data treatment at each stage.
On offboarding the platform MUST provide complete tenant data export in documented formats, followed on request by verifiable deletion.
Platform operators MUST NOT have standing access to tenant business data; access MUST require break-glass per PRD-IAM-011.
Single-tenant and air-gapped deployments MUST use the same tenancy model as multi-tenant, with a single tenant rather than a distinct code path.
Every visual value MUST be a token. Literal values MUST NOT appear in components.
Status tokens MUST be distinguishable without colour, and the data palette MUST be ordered and distinguishable in monochrome and under deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia.
duration-instant MUST be used for any transition on a surface the user is actively working in, and no animation MUST delay the availability of an interactive element.
Density MUST be user-selectable and MUST affect spacing and control size only, never font size below the base.
Identifiers, versions, package identifiers, hashes, and payload fragments MUST be rendered in a monospace face with unambiguous zero, one, and letter forms.
Both themes MUST meet the contrast requirements of INT-UIX-001 independently. Neither MUST be derived by inverting the other.
Theme selection MUST follow the operating system preference by default and MUST be overridable per user, with the choice persisted.
Status colour MUST be consistent across every surface: a severity, a service level state, or a coverage confidence MUST use the same token everywhere it appears.
The interface MUST NOT assume a fixed hierarchy depth or fixed level names, and MUST render tenant-configured node type labels including vocabulary overrides.
Breadcrumbs MUST begin at the caller's scope root and MUST NOT display or imply ancestors outside their scope.
The current scope MUST be visible on every surface that presents scoped data.
Every object MUST be reachable by its human-facing code through the command interface.
Every action available by pointer MUST be available by keyboard. A pointer-only capability MUST NOT exist.
Destructive and irreversible actions MUST require an explicit confirmation that is not the default focus target, and MUST state what will happen rather than asking for generic confirmation.
Optimistic update MUST be used for state changes with a visible reconciliation on failure, and MUST NOT be used where the server may reject on a guard the client cannot evaluate.
Bulk selection MUST state the count and scope of what is selected, MUST distinguish "all on this page" from "all matching the filter", and MUST show the per-item outcome after execution.
Where a bulk operation is partially denied, the interface MUST show which items were denied and why, and MUST NOT present the operation as wholly successful or wholly failed.
The credential field MUST NOT accept a plaintext value. It MUST accept a reference and MUST reject a value with an explanation.
The timeline MUST distinguish actor types — human, service, automation, platform — visually and MUST identify the automation rule where one acted.
Comments attributed through inbound email MUST be visibly marked as such.
Truncated values MUST be recoverable in full without navigation, and truncation MUST NOT be applied to identifiers, versions, or package identifiers.
Unmeasured MUST be visually distinct from zero and from empty.

A restricted field the viewer may not see MUST be absent rather than masked, except where absence would misrepresent the object, in which case a withheld indicator MUST be shown without confirming a value exists.
A degraded capability MUST state which capability, why, and what remains available. An empty region MUST NOT be rendered in its place.
Error presentation MUST NOT include stack traces, framework or dependency versions, internal hostnames, or query fragments.
The honesty surfaces of §10 MUST NOT be suppressible by theme, density, template, or user preference.
Coverage indication MUST be designed to be read rather than tolerated, and its visual weight MUST be validated with the executive audience before release.
Views MUST render progressively, and a slow region MUST NOT delay the surrounding view.
The interface MUST remain usable at 200 ms round-trip latency, and interaction MUST NOT require a round trip where local state suffices.
Responses containing CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data MUST NOT be cached by the browser or an intermediary.
Tablet-class viewports MUST support review and approval workflows. Full practitioner workflows are not required below desktop.

The platform MUST compute a deterministic fingerprint for every finding from attributes that are stable across rescans, and MUST use it to resolve whether an incoming finding is new or an existing record. The fingerprint algorithm MUST be versioned, and the platform MUST support re-fingerprinting with preservation of triage state and history.
Findings from every source — automated ingestion, native matching, manual assessment — MUST pass through one normalization and deduplication pipeline.
A finding MUST be able to affect multiple assets, and the platform MUST report per-asset remediation status independently of the finding's aggregate status.
The platform MUST record the source, tool, tool version, and rule identifier for every finding.
The platform MUST support a tenant-configurable severity taxonomy, with a product-fixed internal ordinal for comparison and normalization across sources.
Severity assigned by a source MUST be retained unmodified, separately from any platform-adjusted or tenant-overridden severity, with adjustments recorded with actor and reason.

The platform MUST enrich findings with available vulnerability intelligence, at minimum: vulnerability identifier, weakness classification, severity scoring, exploit prediction, and known-exploited status.
Enrichment data MUST carry its retrieval timestamp and source version, and stale enrichment MUST be visibly indicated.
The platform MUST support ingestion and application of exploitability statements that assert a known vulnerability is not exploitable in a specific product context.
Finding state transitions MUST follow a defined state machine with recorded actor, timestamp, and reason for every transition.
The platform MUST distinguish closure reasons, at minimum: fixed and verified, fixed and unverified, not applicable, false positive, duplicate, risk accepted, and asset retired.
A finding closed as fixed MUST record the verification method and, where verification occurred, the verifying actor and evidence.
A finding that reappears after closure MUST be reopened as the same record with an incremented recurrence count, not created as a new finding.
The platform MUST support dispute of a finding by the accountable party, with the dispute recorded, routed for adjudication, and the finding's clock behaviour defined during dispute.
False positive determinations MUST be recorded with reason and MUST be usable to suppress recurrence of the same determination on subsequent scans.
The platform MUST support bulk triage operations over filtered finding sets, with per-finding audit records and a defined partial-failure outcome.
The platform MUST support finding-level assignment to an accountable individual, distinct from the asset's owner.
The platform MUST support suggested grouping of related findings for efficient triage, with grouping being advisory and never altering individual finding identity or state.

Findings representing exposed credentials MUST follow a lifecycle in which risk acceptance is unavailable, remediation requires recorded rotation or revocation, the secret value is stored encrypted and displayed only partially masked, and validity checking against the issuing system is supported where feasible.
The platform MUST retain a queryable history of every finding's state, severity, assignment, and score over time.

The platform MUST represent all trackable application security work as a WorkItem aggregate distinguished by type, covering at minimum: assessment and test requests, remediation obligations, exception requests, asset ownership claims, platform engineering tasks, governance and reporting tasks, enablement activities, incident support, and generic tasks.
Work item types MUST be tenant-definable, declaring their field schema, workflow, permission requirements, and default views.
The platform MUST support tenant-defined custom fields per work item type, with typed values, validation, conditional visibility, default values, and inclusion in filtering, search, and export.
The platform MUST support work item templates that pre-populate fields, checklists, and sub-items.
Work items MUST support sub-items and checklists, where sub-item completion is visible on the parent without sub-items being independently scheduled work.
Work items MUST support typed relationships including at minimum blocks, is blocked by, relates to, duplicates, and caused by, with inverse relationships maintained automatically.
Work items MUST support tenant-defined labels, participating in filtering, saved queries, and automation conditions.

Work item workflows MUST be defined as data: states, permitted transitions, transition guards, required fields per state, permission requirements per transition, and side effects. Tenants MUST be able to define and modify workflows per work item type without code change. The platform MUST ship default workflows and MUST validate a workflow for reachability and terminal-state presence before activation.
Workflow definitions MUST be versioned, and in-flight work items MUST continue under the version in effect at their creation unless explicitly migrated.
Every state transition MUST record actor, timestamp, source state, target state, and where required a reason.

The platform MUST maintain an append-only record of every work item state transition, including duration in the prior state and whether any service level clock was running, retained for the life of the work item.
Work items MUST support assignment to a single accountable individual, with additional participants in declared supporting roles.
The platform MUST provide each user a personal work view, prioritized, showing items assigned to them, items awaiting their action, and items they are watching.
The platform MUST provide board views grouped by workflow state, supporting inline transition, with configurable columns and swimlanes.
The platform MUST support saved queries with sharing, and shared queries MUST evaluate against the viewing user's authorized scope rather than the author's.
The platform MUST support bulk operations over filtered work item sets, with per-item audit records, per-item permission evaluation, and a defined partial-failure outcome.
The platform MUST provide keyboard-driven navigation and a command interface for primary actions.
The platform MUST provide full-text search across work items, comments, and custom field values, scope-filtered, with result ranking and filtering.

Work items MUST support: threaded comments with constrained rich text including code formatting; mentions of users and groups that generate notification; watchers with explicit subscribe and unsubscribe; a unified activity timeline interleaving state changes, field changes, comments, attachments, and automated actions in chronological order; attachments on comments; and per-user unread state.
The platform MUST support inbound email association, whereby a reply to a notification is recorded as a comment on the originating work item.
Concurrent edits to the same work item MUST be detected and MUST NOT silently discard either party's change.
The platform MUST autosave in-progress composition of comments and long-form fields.
The platform MUST support lightweight acknowledgement of comments.
The platform MUST support permission configuration at work item type level and at field level within a type.
The platform MUST support deterministic automation rules of condition-action form, evaluated on defined triggers, with every automated action attributed to the rule and recorded in audit.
Automation rules MUST NOT perform an action the rule's owning principal is not authorized to perform, MUST have loop detection, and MUST have a bounded execution budget per trigger.
The platform MUST record effort per work item derived from state duration, and MUST permit optional manual effort adjustment without requiring routine time entry.
Work items MUST support service level policy application with clock pause and recorded blocking attribution.
The platform MUST support lightweight time-boxed planning periods for the security team, with items assigned to a period and completion visible against it.
Work items MUST link to the domain objects they concern — findings, assets, assessments, exceptions — and those objects MUST show their associated work.
Transition evaluation MUST follow the order of §2.1, and a scope failure MUST be indistinguishable from non-existence.
A transition MUST be atomic: state change, transition record, side effects, and event publication in one transaction. A partial transition MUST NOT be observable.
Guard expressions MUST be deterministic, side-effect free, and bounded in evaluation cost. They MUST NOT invoke AI, external services, or unbounded queries.

A workflow definition MUST be validated before activation for: every state reachable from the initial state, at least one terminal state, every non-terminal state having at least one outbound transition, and no transition referencing a state outside the definition.
Fixed machines (§LC-03) MUST NOT be tenant-configurable, and the platform MUST reject an attempt to define a workflow for them.
Returning to a previously occupied state MUST be a distinct forward transition with its own record, never a reversal.
Notification MUST NOT be a transition side effect. Transitions publish events; notification subscribes.
Default workflows MUST include at least one state in each category — open, in progress, waiting external, terminal — so that flow and cycle-time analysis is meaningful without tenant configuration.
Reorganization MUST validate the complete target structure before any mutation, and a failure after mutation MUST compensate by rebuilding the closure from org_node.
hierarchy_version MUST NOT be reused after a failed reorganization.
Where compensation fails, the saga MUST enter a manual-intervention state that blocks further reorganization for the tenant and alerts.
Scope descriptors on existing objects MUST NOT be modified by reorganization.
Concurrent conflicting transitions MUST be resolved by optimistic concurrency with an explicit conflict response. Silent last-write-wins MUST NOT occur.
An automated transition losing to a human transition MUST record the denial rather than retrying or failing silently.
Hierarchy-mutating operations MUST serialize per tenant.
Indirect prompt injection is mitigated, not prevented. Segregation and output validation reduce but do not eliminate the influence of injected content on generated narrative

Authorization enforcement coverage depends on the enforcement point map remaining current. A new egress path added without a map entry is unenforced, and no test detects the absence because the test is the one not written

Score gaming through a consistently wrong baseline is not detected. Controls detect rates of change; a tenant that under-declares criticality and exposure from onboarding produces internally consistent, externally wrong scores

The shared vulnerability intelligence dataset is safe by property, not by control. Its safety rests on containing no tenant data, and a well-meaning addition — prevalence counts, cached match outcomes — would break it without breaking any test
Supply chain compromise cannot be prevented, only detected and evidenced.

Aggregation is an open-ended disclosure channel. §8 addresses the presentations identified; each new aggregate presentation creates a new channel, and the analysis is most likely skipped when the presentation appears innocuous
Every audit event MUST use the fixed envelope with a typed payload. A new event type MUST NOT introduce envelope fields.
The sequence MUST be monotonic and gapless per tenant, and a gap MUST be treated as a verification failure.
Every event MUST record the organizational scope in effect at the time, independently of the current hierarchy.
Actor type MUST distinguish human, service, automation, and platform process, and where an action was performed on behalf of another the initiating principal MUST also be recorded.
denial_reason MUST be recorded at full fidelity and MUST NOT be returned to a client.
The catalogue MUST be maintained as a machine-readable artifact, and every audit-emitting code path MUST reference a catalogued type. An uncatalogued type MUST fail the build.
Every access to RESTRICTED data MUST be recorded at object granularity with the specific object and field.
Configuration changes MUST record before and after values, excluding secret material.
Bulk operations MUST emit an event per item in addition to a summary event.
Read operations on non-restricted data MUST NOT be audited by default.
The canonical serialization MUST be deterministic and versioned, and the version MUST be recorded per event.
The chain MUST be per tenant, and a cross-tenant chain MUST NOT be constructed.

No mechanism MUST exist to modify or delete an audit event: not through the application, the API, administrative tooling, or an operator interface. Deletion MUST be possible only by partition drop under retention (§7).
Chain computation MUST occur in the same transaction as the event insert, and a concurrent insert MUST NOT produce two events with the same sequence or a forked chain.
Checkpoints MUST be created at a configured interval and MUST be anchored to a target outside the platform's control, with the anchor reference recorded and confirmation tracked.
Anchor failure MUST alert and MUST NOT halt audit writing.
Verification MUST be invocable by a tenant over their own trail, and the result MUST be reportable as evidence.
A verification failure MUST alert to a destination outside operator control, MUST be recorded as an audit event, and MUST NOT be suppressible in-product.
Erasure MUST remove only the payload, MUST leave the envelope and chain intact, and MUST record that erasure occurred with its basis.
Verification MUST report erased payloads distinctly from missing or altered data, and MUST NOT report an erased payload as a verification failure.
Erasure MUST require elevated permission distinct from administration, MUST be dual-controlled, MUST record the requesting basis, and MUST be blocked by legal hold.
The envelope MUST NOT contain personal data beyond principal identifiers, which are pseudonymized rather than erased.
Retention MUST be tenant-configurable above a product minimum, and the minimum MUST NOT be configurable downward.
Expiry MUST be implemented as partition drop after archival, and archived events MUST remain verifiable against their checkpoints.
Legal hold MUST be enforced by a register consulted before partition drop and before erasure, not by a per-row flag.
Retention configuration changes MUST be audited and MUST NOT apply retroactively to shorten retention of already-recorded events without a separate elevated action.
Audit read MUST require a permission not implied by administrative permission, and MUST be separately assignable.
Audit queries MUST be scope-filtered against the querying principal's authorized scope.
Audit read MUST itself be audited.
Audit events MUST NOT contain restricted values. A reveal event records that a reveal occurred, never what was revealed.
Break-glass activity MUST be visible to the affected tenant at object granularity, and that visibility MUST NOT be suppressible by the operator.
Audit search MUST return within 5 seconds at p95 over a 12-month range at the Medium profile.
Search MUST support export of a result set as evidence, with the export itself audited and the applied scope and filters recorded in the artifact.
Search MUST NOT support a free-form expression language over the trail.
The platform MUST support continuous export of audit events to a tenant-nominated external system in a documented format, with at-least-once delivery, gap detection, and sequence preservation.
Exported events MUST carry the sequence, chain hash, and envelope so that the external copy is independently verifiable.
Export MUST be residency-constrained per SEC-TEN-018 and MUST exclude payloads where the destination is outside the tenant's residency designation.
An audited operation MUST NOT be acknowledged as successful unless its audit event is durably recorded. Where audit recording fails, the operation MUST fail.
Audit unavailability MUST produce a clear service-unavailable response naming audit as the degraded dependency, not a generic error.
Missing future partitions MUST alert in advance of need and MUST NOT be permitted to cause an insert failure.
The permission catalogue MUST be product-fixed, and every catalogue entry MUST correspond to at least one enforcement point in code. A catalogue entry gating nothing MUST be treated as a defect.
Authorization evaluation MUST NOT branch on role name, role count, role identity, organizational position, or any proxy for seniority. Evaluation MUST resolve a named permission.
Where two actions on a resource differ in consequence such that a tenant might plausibly grant one and not the other, they MUST be separate permissions.
Bulk and export actions MUST be gated by permissions distinct from single-record read.
Access to RESTRICTED data MUST require a permission that is never implied by any other permission, role seniority, or administrative capability.
Roles MUST be composed only from catalogue permissions, and a role MUST NOT be able to reference a permission that does not exist.
Default role templates MUST be materialized per tenant at provisioning with no live link to the template.
A new catalogue permission MUST NOT be added to any existing role automatically.
Role and assignment changes MUST be audited with before and after state, and auz.role.manage and auz.assignment.manage MUST be distinct from every operational permission.
Scope MUST be resolved per permission. Where a principal holds multiple assignments, the result is the union of permission-scope pairs, never the cross product of permissions and scopes.
Scope resolution MUST occur server-side from the authenticated principal and MUST NOT accept any client-supplied scope, node list, or filter as authoritative.

Scope resolution results MAY be cached, and the cache MUST be invalidated explicitly on hierarchy change, assignment change, role change, and node archival, taking effect within the bound of NFR-SEC-002.
Authorization MUST be evaluated through a single contract, and application code MUST NOT implement its own check. Data access MUST be unable to proceed without an evaluation result.
Evaluation MUST deny by default: on no matching grant, on evaluation error, on unavailable scope resolution, and on any unhandled condition.
Every denial MUST emit an audit event with the principal, permission, object reference, and reason.
Collection operations MUST apply the scope predicate as part of retrieval, not as a filter after it. Counts, aggregates, pagination, and relevance MUST be computed post-predicate.

Every operation accepting an object identifier MUST re-validate that object against the principal's resolved scope, independently of how the identifier was obtained, including identifiers returned by a prior response in the same session.
A server-side-filtered selection interface MUST NOT be treated as an authorization control. Every write accepting a selected identifier MUST re-validate it.
Object identifiers MUST NOT be sequential or otherwise predictable, and unpredictability MUST NOT be relied upon as the control.
Responses MUST NOT differentiate non-existence from non-authorization, in status code, error code, message, or timing.
Field-level restrictions MUST be enforced on every representation of the object: single read, collection, search result, export, notification content, API response, and AI context.
A restricted field MUST be absent from the representation, not present with a masked value, where absence is achievable.
Each reveal of a RESTRICTED field MUST emit an audit event naming the specific object and field.

Graph traversal MUST evaluate scope per node reached, and an out-of-scope node MUST terminate that branch. Traversal MUST NOT fail the whole operation, and MUST NOT indicate that a branch was terminated.
Traversal depth and breadth MUST be bounded, and the bound MUST NOT vary with the principal's scope.
Aggregate and comparative presentations MUST enforce a minimum contributing-population size or suppress, and MUST NOT permit derivation of an out-of-scope value by subtraction from a broader total.
A score factor breakdown MUST include only contributions from objects within the requesting principal's scope.

Historical evaluation MUST resolve scope from the object's recorded ScopeDescriptor and the principal's assignments in effect at the evaluation time, never from the current hierarchy or current assignments.
Historical authorization MUST grant read only. It MUST NOT permit any write, and MUST NOT extend to objects created after the evaluation time.
Every report and export MUST state whether it aggregates *as-was* (by descriptor) or *as-is* (by current tree).
Object grants MUST be evaluated independently of scope inheritance and MUST NOT be widened by any change to the hierarchy, role definitions, or node assignments.
Every object grant MUST have a mandatory expiry bounded by a configured maximum, with automatic revocation.

A principal holding only object grants MUST NOT be able to enumerate organization nodes, assets, findings, users, or any object outside the grant — through search, traversal, aggregate, notification content, export, or error differentiation.
Object grants MUST require acceptance of configured agreements before first access, and access before acceptance MUST be impossible rather than merely discouraged.
Service principal scope MUST be pinned to the credential and MUST NOT be derived from a human principal, inherited from an organization node, or asserted in a request payload.
Service principals MUST hold the minimum permission set for their function, and the platform MUST document the minimum set per integration pattern.
Automation rules MUST execute with the authority of their owning principal and MUST NOT effect any change that principal could not perform directly.
Where an automation rule's owning principal loses a permission or has their assignment revoked, rules depending on it MUST be suspended and the owner notified — not silently continued.
Separation-of-duties constraints MUST be enforced both at grant time and at action time.
The platform MUST ship the constraints of §15.1 as default configuration, and relaxing one MUST require elevated permission and be audited.
Exception approval MUST enforce that the approver differs from the requester, as an invariant rather than an advisory check.
dat.erasure.execute MUST require dual control.
Delegation MUST NOT grant a permission or scope the delegator does not hold, MUST be time-bounded, MUST be individually audited, and MUST NOT be re-delegable.
Actions under delegation MUST record both the acting principal and the delegating principal.
The platform MUST answer, for any principal, the complete resolved permission set with scope and the grants producing each — including role assignments, object grants, and delegations.
The platform MUST answer the inverse: for any object or scope, which principals can perform a given permission on it.
Inspection MUST reflect the live evaluation path, computed by the same code, not a parallel reporting implementation.
Inspection output MUST be exportable for periodic access review, and the export MUST be permission-gated and audited.
Every enforcement point in §17 MUST have a test asserting denial for an out-of-scope principal, and a new data egress path MUST NOT be introduced without adding both a map entry and the test.

Continuous integration MUST enforce a static analysis rule rejecting comparison of any role identifier — name, code, or identity — against a literal in application code, and rejecting data access that does not pass through the evaluation contract.
Any exemption from SEC-AUZ-050 MUST be individually annotated with a justification, individually reviewed, and reported so that the exemption count is visible and its growth trackable.
A stewardship grant MUST NOT widen what its holder can see, and MUST NOT be required to expire.
Requesting an assessment of an asset MUST require a stewardship grant over it or an assessment-execution permission, and MUST NOT be satisfied by organization scope alone.
A steward MUST be able to delegate the request capability over their own asset without holding the platform-wide grant permission, and MUST NOT be able to delegate any capability they do not hold.

Composite authority — where an operation is permitted by a platform permission or by a relationship to the specific object — MUST be evaluated in a single named component, and MUST NOT be re-implemented at each call site.

Every deliberately introduced privileged path MUST be recorded in this document with its justification and the specific controls that distinguish it from a backdoor, and a new privileged path MUST NOT be introduced without adding an entry.
The platform MUST detect and alert on volume anomalies in read, export, and RESTRICTED reveal, per principal, against that principal's own baseline.
The platform MUST detect and alert on authorization denial patterns indicating enumeration: sustained denials against sequential or varied identifiers from one principal.

The platform MUST detect and alert on configuration changes affecting authorization, workflow permissions, automation authority, or scoring, and MUST produce a periodic summary regardless of whether an alert fired.
The platform MUST detect and alert on anomalous rates of score-reducing actions per principal and per organization node.
Continuous cross-tenant assertion MUST run in production, not only in test, and MUST alert on any violation.
The platform MUST detect and alert on break-glass invocation, on any grant approaching its bound, and on any attempt to extend one.
Detection alerts MUST be delivered to a destination outside the control of the principal whose activity triggered them.
Every accepted residual risk MUST have a stated revisit trigger expressed as a condition, and MUST be reviewed when the condition occurs rather than on a schedule.

This threat model MUST be revised when a trust boundary is added or changed, when a new external integration or egress path is introduced, when a new data classification appears, when a deliberate privileged path is added, or when a new principal type is introduced.
Each threat scenario in §7 MUST be represented in the platform's own penetration testing scope, and a scenario without a corresponding test objective MUST be recorded as untested.
Test credential protection · Superseded by SEC-PTR-007

The assessment request intake surface MUST enforce: content-signature verification of every attachment against its declared type; malware scanning before an attachment becomes retrievable; storage on an origin distinct from the API with non-inline disposition and server-generated filenames; hardened parsing of uploaded API collections per §11; secret detection on uploaded collections with the result surfaced to the submitter; and per-principal rate limiting on request creation.

Where no secrets store is integrated, the platform MAY take custody of a test account credential submitted with an assessment request, and where it does it MUST: encrypt the value at rest under a key held outside the database; destroy the value in the same transaction as the request's transition to a terminal state; retain a tombstone recording that a credential was held and when it was destroyed; flag the account for rotation at destruction; mask the value by default in every interface with reveal gated by an explicit permission, step-up authentication, and a per-object audit entry; exclude it from every export, notification, report, and AI context without exception; and refuse the submission rather than store the value unencrypted where no key is configured.
Document parsing and vulnerability matching MUST execute in a worker process separate from the API process, with independent resource limits. Parsing MUST NOT occur in a process serving requests.

Every document parser MUST enforce: maximum document size; maximum nesting depth; maximum element and key count; maximum total expanded size; a bounded parse timeout; disabled external reference and entity resolution; safe deserialization with no arbitrary type construction; and rejection rather than truncation on limit breach. Limits MUST be declared per format in the parser registry. Parse failures MUST be logged with a submission identifier and MUST NOT echo document content.

The platform MUST meet ASVS Level 2 across all chapters, with Level 3 in authentication, session management, cryptography, secrets management, and audit logging. Conformance MUST be documented per control, not claimed per level.
Federated authentication via OIDC MUST be the primary method, with local authentication available only where no provider is configured and for break-glass.
Multi-factor authentication MUST be supported, and a tenant policy MUST be able to require it for all principals or for holders of specified permissions.

Step-up authentication MUST be required for restricted-data reveal, elevated exception approval, authorization or workflow configuration change, erasure, and break-glass, with a maximum age of 5 minutes.
Authentication throttling MUST degrade an attacker without permitting lockout of a named principal at will: progressive delay and risk-based challenge rather than account disable.
Credential stuffing controls MUST include breached-credential checking at set and at authentication where local credentials are in use.
Authentication responses MUST NOT differentiate an unknown principal from an incorrect credential, in status, message, or timing.
Every authentication event, success and failure, MUST be recorded with source context.

Session identifiers MUST be generated by a cryptographically secure source with at least 128 bits of entropy, MUST NOT encode any principal or tenant data, and MUST be regenerated on privilege change and on authentication.
Sessions MUST have both absolute and idle lifetime limits, tenant-configurable within product bounds, with a product maximum absolute lifetime of 12 hours.
Session revocation MUST take effect within 60 seconds across every component including cached authorization state, and MUST apply to tokens already issued.
Principals MUST be able to view and terminate their own active sessions with source context.
Session cookies MUST be Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax or stricter, and MUST be scoped to the narrowest applicable path.

Credentials MUST be stored using a memory-hard password hashing function with per-credential salt and parameters tuned to a target verification cost, and parameters MUST be stored alongside so they can be raised without invalidating existing credentials.
Credential policy MUST enforce a minimum length of 12 characters and breached-credential rejection, and MUST NOT enforce composition rules or mandatory periodic rotation.
Credential reset MUST use a single-use, time-limited token delivered out of band, MUST invalidate all sessions on use, and MUST NOT disclose whether the principal exists.
Cryptographic operations MUST use vetted library implementations of current recommended algorithms. Custom cryptographic construction MUST NOT be used.
Data encryption keys MUST be per tenant, wrapped by a key-encryption key held in a hardware-backed or equivalently protected store, and key access MUST be bound to the established tenant context.
Key rotation MUST be supported without downtime, with prior key versions retained for decryption until re-encryption completes, and rotation MUST be schedulable and auditable.
Key material MUST NOT be recoverable by platform operators without break-glass, and key destruction MUST be dual-controlled and audited.
The following MUST be encrypted at rest with tenant key material: test credentials, secret finding values, evidence content, personal workload data, and tenant data exports.
Transport MUST use TLS 1.2 or higher with strong cipher suites; TLS 1.3 MUST be preferred; plaintext HTTP MUST NOT be served except for a redirect.

Secrets MUST be held in a dedicated store with per-tenant namespaces, MUST be referenced by identifier throughout the platform, and MUST NOT appear in any domain table, configuration file, environment variable of a long-lived process, container image, or source repository.
Secrets MUST NOT be retrievable in plaintext after entry except through an explicitly permissioned, step-up-authenticated, per-object-audited reveal operation.

Secret material MUST be excluded from logs, error messages, stack traces, telemetry, exports, notifications, webhook payloads, and AI prompt context. Exclusion MUST be enforced by a redaction layer, not by author discipline.
Secret rotation MUST be supported for every secret type the platform holds, and a rotation failure MUST surface rather than silently retaining the prior value.
Input MUST be validated against a positive schema — type, range, length, format, and permitted values — at the trust boundary, and unknown fields MUST be rejected.
Output encoding MUST be contextual and applied at the point of rendering, not at the point of storage.

Content originating outside the platform MUST be treated as hostile wherever it is rendered. This includes finding titles and descriptions, component names, scanner output, SBOM content, and migrated comments.
Rich text MUST be constrained by an allowlist of permitted elements and attributes. Arbitrary markup MUST NOT be sanitized and accepted.

Uploads MUST be validated by content signature against the declared type, and a mismatch MUST be rejected. Size limits MUST apply per file and per request.

Uploads MUST be malware-scanned before becoming retrievable. A malicious verdict on evidence MUST flag rather than delete, requiring explicit acknowledgement before retrieval; a malicious verdict on any other upload category MUST reject.

Uploaded content MUST be stored with server-generated names on an origin distinct from the API, served only via short-lived signed references with non-inline disposition and content-type enforcement, and MUST NOT be rendered inline under any configuration.
Archive and compressed uploads MUST enforce expansion ratio, entry count, total size, and path containment limits, and MUST reject entries resolving outside the extraction root.
Evidence retention MUST be bounded by a product maximum. Indefinite retention MUST NOT be configurable.
